annotations.text:
TODAY vs THE DESK, same second, one camera lit.

Left is the shipped screen, reproduced from show-phone.html — including its 4:3 map box, which letterboxes a 27 x 45 m house into the middle third. Its honest error is 38.7 / 27.3 / 16.0 % at one, two and three cameras, against a 15-25 % target, and its only two inputs are the win condition and a constant welded shut at 62 degrees.

Right never goes blank. It shows what the house HEARD.

HOW LOUD is the ring, and the metres beside the label — loudness x 14 m, the Hunter's own hearing range.
HOW WELL YOU KNOW WHERE is the core: a dot inside coverage, a band outside it.

The two are independent, which is the trick: a very loud noise you cannot place and a quiet one you can are different readings. That is why the band carries metres too.

One camera lights TWO rooms (coverage.js ROOMS_PER_CAM), so the plans here show four rooms dark at one camera and two at two.

THE THREE WAYS AN HONEST GUIDE IS WRONG — all physical, all pointable-at afterwards.

That is what buys the deniable lie: a guide who says CLEAR into one of these screens is doing what most honest guides do most of the time.

The proposed tuning is 26 / 23 / 20 %, in band from episode 2, with the 20 % as a floor no number of cameras removes — because a Hunter lying in wait makes no sound and a sprinting robot cannot hear one. PROPOSED, not measured: three duty cycles have to be measured first, and one is a stop-ship. If the Hunter's stationary fraction reads under 0.10 the floor collapses and full coverage is an oracle again.

AND THIS IS THE ARGUMENT.

The crash is already public — captions.js ships LOUD CRASH — {ROOM} and broadcast §3 forbids cutting the audio. For the first time the table can say "you had the same crash I did, in the room you sent him into" — and the runner can alibi the guide from something eight people watched: "she was at RUN, of course he couldn't hear."

NO SIGNAL's deepest flaw was never the blank screen. It was that the guide's evidence was unshared, so there was nothing to argue over.
